output: html_notebook

Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models for dementia, with death as the
competing event and attained age as the timescale, mirroring the Cox models in
`CoxPH_B.Rmd`.

**This notebook is for inspecting and validating.** The full run is likely to
exhaust memory inside RStudio - that is what happened for the cancer project.
Run the real analysis from a terminal instead:

```
Rscript fg_project1_ADRD.R main
Rscript fg_project1_ADRD.R svedem
```

Both resume from their CSV if they die partway, so restarting is safe.
See `README_fg_project1_ADRD.md`.

# 1.0 Setup

```{r setup}
source("fg_project1_ADRD.R")
```

# 2.0 Check the machinery before touching real data

Runs the full synthetic test suite. Everything must pass before trusting any
numbers below.

```{r}
# Use the Rscript belonging to the R session that is running this notebook.
# On the Windows VDI, Rscript is not on the system PATH, so calling it by bare
# name would fail here the same way it does in PowerShell.
rscript <- file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript")
test_output <- system2(rscript, "test_fg_project1_ADRD.R", stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE)
cat(test_output, sep = "\n")
```

# 3.0 Load the prepared data

Expects `cox_main_2025_06_06.RData` in this folder, containing `to1po2` and
`to1po2_SveDem_D` as produced by `Calculating_BA_B.Rmd` -> `CoxPH_B.Rmd`.

```{r}
datasets       <- load_prepared_data()
to1po2         <- datasets$to1po2
to1po2_SveDem_D <- datasets$to1po2_SveDem_D
rm(datasets); gc()
```

# 4.0 Inspect the event coding on real data

Exit time and status come from four separate ages - `age_entry`,
`age_dementia`, `age_death`, `age_censor` - on a first-event-wins basis.
`age_dementia` reuses `AgeAtLastDate` unchanged, so dementia timing is
identical to the Cox models; `age_death` is recovered from `DODSDATn`, which is
the piece Cox never needed and `AgeAtLastDate` had overwritten.

Competing events are death **and** other dementia subtypes, because the
registers record only one dementia type per person. Run
`Rscript fg_project1_ADRD.R inspect` first if you have not already.

The counts below should satisfy
`competing_deaths(subtype) = competing_deaths(ADRD) + (ADRD events - subtype events)`,
and `censored` should be identical for every outcome. If not, the timeline is
wrong somewhere.

```{r}
for (spec in main_specs) {
  df <- clean_fg_data(to1po2, spec$event_var, "Main")
  cat("\n---", spec$outcome_label, "---\n")
  print(table(df$fg_status))
  cat("N:", nrow(df), "\n")
  cat("Entry age:", paste(round(range(df$AgeAtFirstDate), 1), collapse = " - "), "\n")
  cat("Exit age :", paste(round(range(df$AgeAtLastDate), 1), collapse = " - "), "\n")
  rm(df); gc()
}
```

Sanity check against the Cox models: the Fine-Gray event count for each outcome
should match `nevent` from the corresponding `coxph` fit in `CoxPH_B.Rmd`,
allowing for the shared complete-case sample used here.

```{r}
comparison <- do.call(rbind, lapply(main_specs, function(spec) {
  df <- clean_fg_data(to1po2, spec$event_var, "Main")
  counts <- fg_counts(df)
  cox_n <- sum(!is.na(to1po2[[spec$event_var]]) & to1po2[[spec$event_var]] == 1)
  rm(df); gc()
  data.frame(
    outcome = spec$outcome_label,
    fg_events = counts$events,
    raw_events_in_data = cox_n,
    dropped_to_missingness = cox_n - counts$events,
    competing_deaths = counts$competing_deaths,
    censored = counts$censored
  )
}))
comparison
```

# 5.0 How large will the expansion be?

The expansion is where the memory goes. Check it on the smallest outcome first
to get a feel for the blow-up factor before committing to a full run.

```{r}
probe <- clean_fg_data(to1po2, "Vascular", "Main")
probe_start <- Sys.time()
probe_expanded <- expand_fg_data(probe)

cat("Input rows   :", nrow(probe), "\n")
cat("Expanded rows:", nrow(probe_expanded), "\n")
cat("Blow-up      :", round(nrow(probe_expanded) / nrow(probe), 1), "x\n")
cat("Elapsed      :", round(elapsed_min(probe_start), 2), "min\n")
cat("Approx size  :", round(as.numeric(object.size(probe_expanded)) / 1e9, 2), "Gb\n")
print(summary(probe_expanded$fgwt))
```

If that size is uncomfortable, the escape hatch is `fg_config$time_round_digits`
(see section 8.0) - but try the exact run first.

```{r}
rm(probe, probe_expanded); gc()
```

# 6.0 Verify the one-expansion-per-outcome shortcut on real data

Each outcome is expanded **once** and all four models (2 BA measures x 2
adjustment sets) are fitted on that single expansion. This is valid only
because `finegray()` weights depend on `(entry, exit, status, id)` and not on
the covariates carried along. The test suite checks this on synthetic data;
this confirms it on the real cohort.

```{r}
verify_expansion_invariance <- function(data, event_var, dataset_label) {
  df <- clean_fg_data(data, event_var, dataset_label)
  full    <- expand_fg_data(df)
  minimal <- expand_fg_data(df, ba_measures = fg_config$ba_measures[1],
                            covariates = "gender")
  result <- c(
    same_rows    = nrow(full) == nrow(minimal),
    same_weights = isTRUE(all.equal(full$fgwt, minimal$fgwt)),
    same_start   = isTRUE(all.equal(full$fgstart, minimal$fgstart)),
    same_stop    = isTRUE(all.equal(full$fgstop, minimal$fgstop))
  )
  rm(df, full, minimal); gc()
  result
}

verify_expansion_invariance(to1po2, "Vascular", "Main")
```

All four must be `TRUE`. If any is `FALSE`, stop and expand per model instead.

# 7.0 Single-outcome trial run

Run one outcome end to end to confirm timing and memory before launching
everything. Results append to a scratch CSV.

```{r}
trial_file <- "finegray_project1_TRIAL.csv"

run_outcome_block(
  data          = to1po2,
  specs         = main_specs,
  dataset_label = "Main",
  results_file  = trial_file,
  only_outcomes = "Vascular"
)

read.table(trial_file, sep = ";", dec = ",", header = TRUE,
           quote = "", fileEncoding = "Latin1")
```

Multiply the elapsed time by 4 (main) and 10 (SveDem) for a rough total.

# 8.0 Memory escape hatch

Only if the exact run cannot complete. Rounding the exit age collapses tied
event times and shrinks the expansion. Report anything run this way as a
sensitivity analysis, not as the primary result.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# 3 ~ one day, 2 ~ four days, 1 ~ five weeks.
fg_config$time_round_digits <- 2

# Then compare against the exact result for one outcome to see how much
# the estimates actually move before applying it everywhere.
```

# 9.0 Full run

Prefer the terminal scripts. This chunk is `eval=FALSE` on purpose - running it
inside RStudio is what ran out of memory last time.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
run_outcome_block(to1po2, main_specs, "Main", "finegray_project1_main.csv")
run_outcome_block(to1po2_SveDem_D, svedem_specs, "SveDem", "finegray_project1_svedem.csv")
```

# 10.0 Collect results

```{r}
read_results <- function(file) {
  if (!file.exists(file)) return(NULL)
  read.table(file, sep = ";", dec = ",", header = TRUE, quote = "",
             fileEncoding = "Latin1")
}

combined <- do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), list(
  read_results("finegray_project1_main.csv"),
  read_results("finegray_project1_svedem.csv")
)))

if (!is.null(combined)) {
  write.table(combined, "finegray_project1_combined.csv",
              sep = ";", dec = ",", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE,
              fileEncoding = "Latin1")
}
combined
```

# 11.0 What failed and what it cost

```{r}
if (!is.null(combined)) {
  failed <- combined[!is.na(combined$error), ]
  cat("Models attempted:", nrow(combined), "\n")
  cat("Failed:", nrow(failed), "\n")
  if (nrow(failed) > 0) print(failed[, c("dataset", "outcome", "model", "BA", "error")])

  cat("\nModels using the non-robust fallback:",
      sum(combined$robust %in% c(FALSE, "FALSE")), "\n")

  cat("\nSlowest expansions:\n")
  timing <- unique(combined[, c("dataset", "outcome", "fg_expanded_N",
                                "expansion_elapsed_min")])
  print(head(timing[order(-timing$expansion_elapsed_min), ], 10))

  cat("\nTotal model time (min):", round(sum(combined$model_elapsed_min, na.rm = TRUE), 1), "\n")
  cat("Total expansion time (min):", round(sum(timing$expansion_elapsed_min, na.rm = TRUE), 1), "\n")
}
```
